title: The Caribbean as the beginning of the slave trade
summary: He explains slave ships and trade winds carrying slaves to the Caribbean for processing.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That's another thing, too. When people protest about that word, "Negro" -- if you're going to say it in Spanish, it's the same thing. What people don't realize, especially the American Negroes (if you want to call them Negroes)...Blacks... They were processed in the Caribbean. I mean, that was the beginning of the New World. You know, Columbus never touched the mainland, you must understand. When you talk about the trade winds... You know, when the slave ships came, whichever, the way the winds blew, it blew the ships downward to that area of the planet. So therefore, everything started there, really, and the slaves were processed from there and then brought to the mainland. Of course, the Portuguese went a little further down with the trade winds. They went down to South America. See what I mean? And you don't have any records of Negroes being up by where the Pilgrims came. They came at it from another direction.
Of course, if Leif Ericsson in the year 1000 turned south, had been able to go south, we would be speaking Norwegian.
